School locations from VicData's schools table
method.geography: The school against the comparison set shown in 'Compared against' (by default the 10 nearest schools of the same sector, phase and a compatible gender; at Post-16 the 10 nearest with Post-16 results in either of the latest two years).
method.years: The span you choose with 'From'; on points and rates from 2022/23.
leftOut: At GCSE, an independent school whose latest published English and maths grade 4+ figure is 0% while its Attainment 8 is above 5 is treated as sitting IGCSEs (which DfE's tables don't count) and is dropped from every comparison set; a saved or chosen list is not refilled, so a '10 nearest' set can hold fewer than 10. The school itself is kept, but its whole-school headline history is withheld.

A comparison school with no published figure for what is compared (often a school that does not offer the subject) is not listed; one with history but no figure in the latest year is not ranked. Never ranked last.

At GCSE only GCSE (9-1) Full Course entries carry points: another qualification in the same subject (BTEC, Cambridge National, Double Award) shows no points of its own rather than borrowing the GCSE score.

A grade rate is worked out only on the scale it belongs to: Grade 4+ on GCSE 9-1 and Double Award pairs (both digits 4 or above); A*–E on the A-level scale at Post-16. Vocational, IB, T Level and Pre-U rows get no figure.
Non-grades (Suppressed, No result, X, Covid impacted, COVID result, Supp, Not Awarded) are left out of both sides of every grade share.
On a Grade counts selection a school with fewer than 5 graded entries reads 'too few entries' and is not ranked.
Leading and trailing years with no published figure are dropped (2020/21 has no points nationally: grades were teacher-assessed).
Not drawn for a national or regional ranking.
Needs 2 or more years.
Schools with no recorded location are not plotted.
steps: Each school's figure is: with a subject in focus, its entries in the subject (Candidates) or its result in the subject — average points (GCSE: GCSE (9-1) Full Course points; Post-16: the same exact qualification), or a grade rate scored from that school's own grade counts for the same subject and qualification; with no subject, Attainment 8 (GCSE) or A-level average points per entry (Post-16), or the number of pupils at the end of Key stage 4 / 16 to 18 students.
For each school we work out the change over the span: a percentage change on entries; on results the difference in points or percentage points, from 2022/23.
Each dot is coloured by that change on one scale centred on zero: green for the biggest rise in the set, red for the biggest fall, pale amber for little change.
Dot size is the school's entries in the last year.
